title: ihave_push.rs dot_stuff splits on LF but NNTP articles use CRLF: CRLF lines gain extra LF
description:
## What / Why
crates/transit/src/import/ihave_push.rs dot_stuff() splits input on '
' and then re-adds '
' after each line. For CRLF-encoded articles (which is the canonical format per RFC 5536), this means each line with '
' is split into a ''-suffixed segment and the '
' is then re-appended, producing correct output. However, the trailing-newline cleanup logic (pop the final '
' if input doesn't end with '
') can misfire: if article_bytes ends with '
', the final split element is empty (''), and the function adds a '
' for it, then removes it—but the '' from the last real line is left dangling without its matching '
'. This corrupts the last line of the NNTP stream.

## Trigger → Bad Behavior
Import an article file whose last line ends exactly with '
' (standard CRLF article) → send_ihave sends a truncated or malformed last line → transit daemon may reject the article or silently corrupt it.

## Fix
Rewrite dot_stuff to handle CRLF-terminated lines explicitly (split on '
', rejoin with '
'), matching the behavior in fetch.rs which handles this correctly.
